extra.test_case: Light both lamps together and confirm intensity does not exceed the maximum.

extra.text: When an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the requirements for minimum intensity if either lamp has failed.
extra.test_case: Disable each lamp in turn and confirm the remaining lamp meets minimum intensity.

extra.text: An interdependent lamp system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
extra.test_case: Operate all interdependent lamps together and verify photometric and colorimetric compliance.

extra.text: If the interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility colorimetric and photometric requirement, at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
extra.test_case: Test the specified interdependent lamps at all fixed positions of the movable component for outboard visibility, colour and photometry.

extra.text: The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
extra.test_case: Operate the variable intensity control across its range and confirm intensities stay within paragraph 5 limits.

extra.text: The variable intensity control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5. for the specific lamp: (a) for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions: under night-time conditions; (b) for other systems: under standard conditions.
extra.test_case: Under night-time or standard conditions, confirm intensity does not exceed the steady-lamp maximum.

extra.text: If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously and the intensity of the rear position lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table.
extra.test_case: Measure combined and position-only intensities within ±5° V / ±10° H and confirm ratio ≥5:1 at each point.

extra.text: Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities shall be carried out according to Annex 8.
extra.test_case: Verify luminous intensity tests followed the Annex 8 procedure.

extra.text: To check the colorimetric characteristics, the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8. shall be applied.
extra.test_case: Verify colorimetric tests used the paragraph 4.8 test conditions.

extra.text: For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.
extra.test_case: Confirm colour measurements were made with the LED sources installed in the lamp.

extra.text: For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be checked for each light source technology separately according to the applicable provisions in paragraphs 4.8.1. and 4.8.2.
extra.test_case: Measure colour separately for each light source technology and confirm compliance.

extra.text: For rear position lamps of category R1 (steady), the light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4∙10^0 cd, a maximum luminous intensity of 1.7∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp or 8.5∙10^0 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", a standard light distribution according to Figure A3-I, and a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1, as specified in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Measure both samples: HV ≥4 cd, max ≤17 cd (8.5 cd if "D"), Figure A3-I grid compliant, ≥0.05 cd within Table A2-1 angles.

extra.text: For rear position lamps of category R2 (variable), the light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall have a minimum luminous intensity of 4∙10^0 cd, a maximum luminous intensity of 4.2∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp or 2.1∙10^1 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", a standard light distribution according to Figure A3-I, and a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10^-2 cd within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1, as specified in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Measure both samples: HV ≥4 cd, max ≤42 cd (21 cd if "D"), Figure A3-I grid compliant, ≥0.05 cd within Table A2-1 angles.

extra.text: The minimum luminous intensity of the rear position lamp within the angles of geometric visibility shall be as specified in Table 4 (5∙10^-2 cd).
extra.test_case: Measure across Table A2-1 geometric visibility angles and confirm ≥0.05 cd.

extra.text: The rear position lamp shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
extra.test_case: Assess the rear position lamp against paragraph 4.6 failure provisions.

extra.text: For a stop lamp of category S1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd, the maximum luminous intensity shall be 2.60∙10^2 cd when used as a single lamp or 1.30∙10^2 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I and the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility (Table A2-1) shall be 3∙10^-1 cd, as given in Table 7.
extra.test_case: Measure intensity in reference axis, standard light distribution points and geometric visibility field; verify ≥60 cd, ≤260 cd (≤130 cd if 'D'), and ≥0.3 cd within Table A2-1 angles.

extra.text: For a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd, the maximum luminous intensity shall be 7.30∙10^2 cd when used as a single lamp or 3.65∙10^2 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I and the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility (Table A2-1) shall be 3∙10^-1 cd (day) and 7∙10^-2 cd (night), as given in Table 7.
extra.test_case: Measure in day and night modes; verify ≥60 cd, ≤730 cd (≤365 cd if 'D'), and ≥0.3 cd day / ≥0.07 cd night within Table A2-1 angles.

extra.text: For a stop lamp of category S3 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 2.5∙10^1 cd, the maximum luminous intensity shall be 1.10∙10^2 cd when used as a single lamp or 5.5∙10^1 cd when used as a lamp marked "D", the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-III and the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility (Table A2-1) shall be 3∙10^-1 cd, as given in Table 7.
extra.test_case: Measure per Figure A3-III; verify ≥25 cd, ≤110 cd (≤55 cd if 'D'), ≥0.3 cd within geometric visibility.

extra.text: For a reversing lamp of category AR, the minimum luminous intensity shall be 8.0∙10^1 cd, with the standard light distribution as defined in Figure A3-V, as given in Table 10.
extra.test_case: Measure in reference axis and Figure A3-V points; verify minimum ≥80 cd per distribution.

extra.text: For a reversing lamp of category AR, the maximum luminous intensity in or above the H-plane shall be 3.00∙10^2 cd, as given in Table 10.
extra.test_case: Measure intensity in and above H-plane; verify ≤300 cd.

extra.text: For a reversing lamp of category AR, the maximum luminous intensity below the H-plane, down to 5°D, shall be 6.00∙10^2 cd, as given in Table 10.
extra.test_case: Measure intensity between H-plane and 5°D; verify ≤600 cd.

extra.text: The singular rear position lamp (MR) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 80° inboard / 80° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm), as given in Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the apparent surface is visible over 80°/80° horizontally and 15°/10° vertically, or 15°/5° below 750 mm.

extra.text: The rear position lamps (MR) installed as a pair shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 20° inboard / 80° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm), as given in Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the apparent surface is visible over 20°/80° horizontally and 15°/10° vertically, or 15°/5° below 750 mm.

extra.text: The rear position lamp (R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard (20°/80° reduced angles used only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm). It shall have minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 15° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm; 5°/15° for optional lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm), as given in Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Measure the geometric visibility of the rear position lamp apparent surface on a goniometer and confirm it is unobstructed over at least 45°/80° horizontally and 15°/15° vertically, or the reduced angles applicable to the mounting height.

extra.text: The singular stop lamp (MS) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 45° outboard and minimum vertical angles of 15° above / 10° below (15°/5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm), as given in Table A2-1.
extra.test_case: Verify on a goniometer that the apparent surface is visible over 45°/45° horizontally and 15°/10° vertically, or 15°/5° below 750 mm.

extra.text: The rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp shall meet, for the various directions of measurement relative to the reference axis (H = 0°, V = 0°, passing through the centre of reference), the minimum intensities given in Figures A3-I to A3-XV as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits, unless specified otherwise.
extra.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at each grid direction; each measured intensity ≥ the figure percentage × required minimum, rounded down to three significant digits.

extra.text: Where the rear position lamp or the stop lamp of category S1, S2 or MS is intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: Check manufacturer-declared mounting height; if ≤ 750 mm, verify that photometric compliance is demonstrated down to 5° below horizontal.

extra.text: The rear position lamps and stop lamps of category S1 or S2 shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-I, the values shown giving, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Tables 4 and 7).
extra.test_case: Measure rear position and stop lamp intensities at Figure A3-I points; each ≥ given percentage of the table minimum.

extra.text: The reversing lamp shall meet the standard light distribution of Figure A3-V, the values shown giving, for the various directions of measurement relative to the axis of reference, the minimum intensities in cd.
extra.test_case: Measure reversing lamp intensities at each Figure A3-V point; each ≥ the cd value shown.

extra.text: The conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and a geometric standpoint, in accordance with the requirements of this Regulation, if any, if the differences of the lamp do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
extra.test_case: Compare mechanical and geometric features of randomly sampled production lamps with the approved type; pass if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

extra.text: With respect to photometric performance, when testing the photometric performances set forth in paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation of any lamp chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Measure photometric performance of randomly chosen production rear position, stop and reversing lamps per paragraph 4.8.; pass if no value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3.

extra.text: In the case of a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source, if results of the photometric test do not meet the requirements, tests on lamps shall be repeated using another standard light source.
extra.test_case: If a lamp with replaceable light source fails photometry, repeat the photometric test with another standard light source and check compliance.

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates of the lamp shall be complied with when tested under conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Measure chromaticity coordinates of the red (position, stop) and white (reversing) light of sampled lamps under paragraph 4.9. conditions; pass if within the prescribed colour boundaries.

extra.text: For lamps (functions) using incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after photometric stability shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
extra.test_case: Operate the lamp until photometric stability and measure luminous intensities at all test points; all values must be within the minimum and maximum limits.

extra.text: For the rear position lamp, the luminous intensity distribution shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at 4 seconds after switch ON, using HV as reference coordinate, as listed in Table A8-1.
extra.test_case: Measure HV intensity 4 s after switch ON and scale the distribution by the HV ratio; all test points must meet the rear position lamp min/max limits.

extra.text: For the reversing lamp, the luminous intensity distribution shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, using HV as reference coordinate, as listed in Table A8-1.
extra.test_case: Measure HV intensity 0.2 s after switch ON and scale the distribution by the HV ratio; all test points must meet the reversing lamp min/max limits.

extra.text: In case a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, the lamp (function) is deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time, if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2. are compliant.
extra.test_case: Confirm all lamp functions use LED technology only and that measurements per paragraph 1.2 are compliant; additional time-point testing then not required.

extra.text: In case a lamp (function) uses any other light generating technology, the corresponding intensity requirements of the lamp (function) shall be tested and checked for compliance at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
extra.test_case: Measure intensities from the Table A8-1 time point until photometric stability; all values must be within min/max limits.

extra.text: In case a lamp (function) uses more than one light generating technology, the corresponding intensity requirements of the lamp (function) shall be tested following the strictest time requirements according to paragraphs 2.1.1. to 2.1.3. for the combination of them and checked for compliance.
extra.test_case: Apply the strictest time requirements of 2.1.1 to 2.1.3 and verify intensities comply with min/max limits.

extra.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the corresponding minimum intensity requirements of a lamp (function) shall be tested and checked for compliance at all points in time starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
extra.test_case: If run-up behaviour is doubtful, continuously measure intensity from the Table A8-1 time point to photometric stability; minimum values must be met throughout.

extra.text: A separate approval is required for each retro-reflective device listed in paragraph 1 (the retro-reflector of Class IA or IB).
extra.test_case: Check that the integrated retro-reflector has its own R150 approval, separate from the lamp functions' approvals.

extra.text: The approval number assigned to the approved type of retro-reflector shall be marked on the device following the requirements of paragraph 3.3.
extra.test_case: Inspect the device and verify that the assigned approval number is marked in line with paragraph 3.3.

extra.text: With regard to the size of the approval marking, the value for "a" shall be as defined in Table 1 (minimum 5 mm for retro-reflectors of Class IA or IB).
extra.test_case: Measure the approval mark and verify that dimension "a" is at least 5 mm.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for a circle enclosing "E" and the approving country number.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for the 4- to 6-digit sequential number of the approval.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5 (IA or IB).
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for the correct class symbol (IA or IB) as per Table 1.

extra.text: The approval marking shall consist of the number of this Regulation followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
extra.test_case: Inspect the marking for "150R" followed by the two-digit series of amendments.

extra.text: In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, the retro-reflective device shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: If rotation is restricted, verify that "TOP" is inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the marking shall be visible after their installation.
extra.test_case: Install the lamp on a representative vehicle or fixture and verify that the single approval mark remains visible.

extra.text: Where a single approval mark is affixed on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
extra.test_case: Review the construction to confirm that every light-transmitting part cannot be removed without removing the single approval mark.

extra.text: The requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections of UN Regulation No. 48, and its series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, shall apply to the retro-reflector where its verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
extra.test_case: Check the retro-reflector against the applicable UN R48 sections 5 and 6 provisions for M1 vehicles that can be verified at component approval; all must be met.

extra.text: After verification of the general specifications (paragraph 4.) and the specifications of shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten samples of the retro-reflector shall be subjected to the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6 and, at least one hour after this test, examined as to their colorimetric characteristics in paragraph 5.1.5. and RI in paragraph 5.1.4., for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
extra.test_case: Run the Annex 6 Part 1 heat test on the ten samples and measure colour and RI at 20' and 0°/0° at least one hour later; they must meet 5.1.4 and 5.1.5.

extra.text: The two samples of the first group of retro-reflectors shall be subjected successively to the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) and then, if this test is satisfactory, to the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).
extra.test_case: Perform the water penetration test, then the fuel and lubricant resistance tests on group 1; the samples must pass.

extra.text: The two samples of the second group of retro-reflectors shall, if necessary, be subjected to the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6, and then to the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
extra.test_case: Perform the corrosion test (if applicable) and the rear-face abrasion test on group 2; the samples must pass.

extra.text: The two samples of the third group of retro-reflectors shall be subjected to the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Perform the Annex 4 Part 3 stability-in-time test on group 3; the samples must pass.

extra.text: The two samples of the fourth group of retro-reflectors shall be subjected to the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).
extra.test_case: Perform the Annex 6 Part 6 weathering test on group 4; the samples must pass.

extra.text: After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group must have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.
extra.test_case: Measure the colour of each group after testing; it must meet paragraph 5.1.5.

extra.text: Where more than one axis of reference, or a range of axes of reference, is specified by the manufacturer, the photometric measurements of the retro-reflector shall be repeated, making reference each time to a different axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the range specified by the manufacturer.
extra.test_case: Repeat the photometry for each specified axis or the extreme axes of the range; each set must meet Table 3.

extra.text: The manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the area of the retro-reflector to be used for photometric measurements.
extra.test_case: Check that the drawings define the perimeter of the photometric area.

extra.text: Where the Class IA or Class IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values are verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
extra.test_case: If the mounting height is <750 mm, verify the RI values down to 5° below horizontal only; they must meet Table 3.

extra.text: The testing of the colour for the retro-reflector (night-time colour) shall be carried out according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
extra.test_case: Confirm the colour test report follows the 4.2.1 method.

extra.text: The retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB shall be subjected to the tests in the chronological order given in Table 4 (Chronological order of tests, Classes IA, IB, IIIA and IIIB).
extra.test_case: Review the test report and confirm the samples a to j were tested in the sequence and allocation of Table 4.

extra.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall withstand the heat test according to Part 1 of Annex 6 (48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C) without distortion on visual inspection.
extra.test_case: Expose the samples for 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C and visually inspect; pass if no distortion is visible.

extra.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall withstand the water test according to Part 3 of Annex 6 (10 min in normal position and 10 min in inverted position) followed by visual inspection, colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Immerse the samples 10 min normal and 10 min inverted, inspect, then check colour and photometry; pass if no water ingress and the values are met.

extra.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall withstand the motor fuels test according to Part 1 of Annex 7 (5 min) on visual inspection.
extra.test_case: Expose the samples to motor fuel for 5 min and visually inspect; pass if no visible deterioration.

extra.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall withstand the oils test according to Part 2 of Annex 7 (5 min) on visual inspection, followed by colorimetry and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Expose the samples to lubricating oil for 5 min, inspect, then check colour and photometry; pass if no deterioration and the values are met.

extra.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall withstand the corrosion test according to Part 4 of Annex 6 (24 hours, 2 hours interval, 24 hours) on visual inspection.
extra.test_case: Perform salt-spray exposure 24 h + 2 h interval + 24 h and visually inspect; pass if no corrosion that impairs performance.

extra.text: The retro-reflector samples of Classes IA and IB shall meet the general specifications and the shapes and dimensions of Annex 5 by visual inspection, as listed in Table 4.
extra.test_case: Visually inspect all ten samples against paragraph 4 and Annex 5; pass if no non-conformity is found.

extra.text: After the heat test, the retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall meet the colorimetry requirements of paragraph 4.2. (visual inspection, trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt) and the photometry requirements of Part 1 of Annex 4 limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°, with complete photometry on the designated samples.
extra.test_case: Measure colour and the coefficient of luminous intensity at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° (and complete photometry on two samples); pass if within the required limits.

extra.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall meet the stability in time test according to Part 3 of Annex 4, followed by colorimetry according to paragraph 4.2. and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Perform the stability-in-time test, then check colour and photometry; pass if the values remain within the required limits.

extra.text: The retro-reflector of Classes IA and IB shall meet the resistance to weathering test according to Part 6 of Annex 6, followed by colorimetry according to paragraph 4.2. and photometry limited to 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Perform the weathering exposure, then check colour and photometry; pass if the values remain within the required limits.

extra.text: The chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall be complied with.
extra.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of a randomly chosen production retro-reflector and confirm that they lie within the prescribed red colour boundaries.

extra.text: One of the retro-reflectors of sample A, after the sampling procedure in paragraph 2., shall be tested for resistance to water penetration according to the procedure described in paragraph 1. of Part 2 of Annex 6 and shall pass the test; if the test on sample A is not complied with, both retro-reflective devices of sample B shall pass the same procedure.
extra.test_case: Subject a production retro-reflector sample to the Annex 6 Part 2 paragraph 1 water penetration test and confirm that it passes, or that both sample B devices pass if the first fails.

extra.text: When the RI of the retro-reflective device is measured for an angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be ascertained whether any mirror effect is produced by slightly turning the device; if there is any such effect, a reading shall be taken with an angle β of β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
extra.test_case: Turn the device slightly at β1 = β2 = 0° on the goniometer; if a mirror effect occurs, verify that a reading at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° is taken and recorded.

extra.text: When the RI of a retro-reflective device not marked "TOP" is measured for the other angles of illumination and divergence, the retro-reflective device shall be placed in the position corresponding to the value of ε of minimum RI; if the specified values are not attained, the device may be rotated about its axis of reference ±5° from that position.
extra.test_case: Measure RI at all other specified angles with the device fixed at the minimum-RI ε position (±5° allowed) and verify all values meet the specified limits.

extra.text: If for the direction β1 = β2 = 0°, and for ε = 0° the RI of the retro-reflective device exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.
extra.test_case: Measure RI at β = 0°, ε = 0°; if it is ≥150 % of the specified value, verify all further measurements are made at ε = 0° and meet the limits.

extra.text: For testing the retro-reflection the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with a CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
extra.test_case: Verify the test report shows illumination with CIE Standard Illuminant A and measurement per Annex 4 Part 1.

extra.text: The measuring distance for photometry of the retro-reflective device shall be chosen such that at least the limits for the angles δ, γ and η are respected, but not lower than 10 m.
extra.test_case: Check the test set-up records a measuring distance of at least 10 m with δ ≤ 10', γ ≤ 10' and η ≤ 80'.

extra.text: In the case of moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA, IB, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
extra.test_case: Condition the retro-reflector 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C dry, cool 1 h at 23 °C ± 2 °C, and confirm test conditions were met before inspection.

extra.text: The retro-reflective device, whether part of a lamp or not, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C, the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface being 20 mm below the surface of the water; this test shall be repeated after turning the retro-reflective device through 180°, and the device shall then be immediately immersed in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
extra.test_case: Immerse the stripped retro-reflector 10 min at 50 °C ± 5 °C 20 mm below surface, repeat inverted, then immerse at 25 °C ± 5 °C; verify conditions recorded.

extra.text: If visual inspection does not reveal the presence of water or in case of doubt, in the case of retro-reflectors, the RI shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, the retro-reflective device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
extra.test_case: After lightly shaking off excess water, measure RI per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. and check compliance with its criteria.

extra.text: For retro-reflective devices of the Classes IB and IIIB, as an alternative test procedure of resistance to water penetration and at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture and dust test shall be applied.
extra.test_case: Check the test report shows the moisture test and dust exposure test were performed per Annex 6 Part 3 when the alternative procedure was requested.

extra.text: During the moisture test, the precipitation rate of the water spray at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min as measured with a vertical cylindrical collector centred on the vertical axis of the rotating test platform.
extra.test_case: Verify the collector measurement recorded in the test report is within 2.5 to 4.1 mm/min.

extra.text: During the water spray test, all drain holes and other openings of the device shall remain open and drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
extra.test_case: Inspect the test set-up: all drain holes/openings are unobstructed and any drain wicks are fitted in the device.

extra.text: During the water spray test, the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.
extra.test_case: Verify the recorded platform rotational speed is between 3.5 and 4.5 min-1.

extra.text: If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF during the water spray test.
extra.test_case: Check the test log shows the grouped rear position, stop and reversing lamps operated at design voltage in 5 min ON / 55 min OFF cycles.

extra.text: The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
extra.test_case: Verify the test log shows 12 hours of water spray exposure comprising 12 cycles.

extra.text: After the water spray test, the rotation and the water spray shall be turned OFF and the device allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed.
extra.test_case: Verify the test log records a 1 hour drain period with spray and rotation off and cabinet door closed.

extra.text: Upon completion of the drain period, no standing pool of water shall be allowed to be formed in the interior of the device, or which can be formed by tapping or tilting the device.
extra.test_case: Visually inspect the device interior after draining, including tapping and tilting; pass if no standing pool of water forms.

extra.text: Upon completion of the drain period, the RI shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after having dried the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth.
extra.test_case: Dry the exterior with a cotton cloth and measure RI per Annex 4 Part 1; compare with initial RI and record.

extra.text: The test dust used for the dust exposure test shall be fine powdered cement in accordance with standard ASTM C 150-84.
extra.test_case: Check the test report identifies the dust as ASTM C 150-84 fine powdered cement.

extra.text: The mounted device shall be placed in the dust chamber no closer than 150 mm from a wall and the test dust shall be agitated by compressed air or blower(s) at intervals of 15 min for a period of 2 to 15 s for the duration of 5 hours, the dust being allowed to settle between the agitation periods.
extra.test_case: Verify the test log: device ≥150 mm from walls, agitation of 2-15 s every 15 min over 5 hours.

extra.text: Upon completion of the dust exposure test, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the RI measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Clean and dry the exterior, measure RI per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 and verify the result meets that paragraph's criterion.

extra.text: The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.
extra.test_case: Expose the rear lamp with integrated retro-reflector, stripped of removable parts, to 2 x 24 h saline mist separated by a 2 h drying interval and check test records.

extra.text: After the corrosion test, the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas, when measured after a recovery period of 48 hours as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at an entrance angle of β2 = 5° and an observation angle of α = 20', shall be not less than the value in Table 9 or more than the value in Table 10 respectively, the surface being cleaned to remove salt deposits from the saline mist before measuring.
extra.test_case: After 48 h recovery and cleaning of salt deposits, measure RA at β2 = 5°, α = 20'; pass if within Table 9 / Table 10 limits.

extra.text: For mirror-backed moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB with an accessible rear face, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.
extra.test_case: Check test records that the rear face was brushed with a hard nylon brush.

extra.text: After having brushed the rear face of a moulded plastics reflector of Class IA or IB, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the said rear face for one minute, then removed and the retro-reflective device left to dry.
extra.test_case: Apply a cotton cloth soaked in the Annex 7 Part 1 mixture to the rear face for 1 min, remove and let dry; verify in test records.

extra.text: As soon as evaporation is completed, the reverse side of the mirror-backed retro-reflective device shall be brushed with the same brush as before.
extra.test_case: Verify the rear face was re-brushed with the same hard nylon brush after evaporation.

extra.text: The RI of the mirror-backed retro-reflective device shall then be measured, according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation, after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.
extra.test_case: Cover the rear face with Indian ink and measure RI per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2.; pass if the values meet the requirements of the Regulation.

extra.text: For resistance to fuels, a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol shall be applied to the retro-reflective device.
extra.test_case: Check the test report confirms that a 70 % n-heptane / 30 % toluol mixture was used for the fuel resistance test of the retro-reflector.

extra.text: After about five minutes from wiping with the test mixture, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be inspected visually and must not show any apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.
extra.test_case: Visually inspect the wiped surface after about 5 minutes; pass if no apparent surface changes other than slight surface cracks.

extra.text: For resistance to fuels, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture.
extra.test_case: Wipe the retro-reflector outer and illuminating surfaces lightly with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture and record the procedure.

extra.text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil to test resistance to lubricating oils.
extra.test_case: Wipe the outer and illuminating surface of a moulded PMMA retro-reflector sample with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil and check that the procedure was applied as specified.

extra.text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, after the lubricating oil resistance test, the RI of the retro-reflective device shall be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
extra.test_case: Measure the coefficient of luminous intensity (RI) after the oil test per paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. Pass if the values meet the criteria of that paragraph.

extra.text: For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA and IB, after about 5 minutes of exposure to the detergent lubricating oil, the surface of the retro-reflective device shall be cleaned.
extra.test_case: After about 5 minutes of oil exposure, clean the surface and check by inspection that no oil residue remains before measurement.

extra.text: The approval number on the retro-reflective device must be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
extra.test_case: Inspect the approval mark on the retro-reflector and check that the approval number is placed close to the circle surrounding the letter "E".

extra.text: The digits constituting the approval number of the retro-reflective device must face the same way as the "E".
extra.test_case: Inspect the approval mark and check that the approval number digits are oriented the same way as the letter "E".

extra.text: The group of symbols indicating the class of the retro-reflective device must be diametrically opposite the approval number.
extra.test_case: Inspect the approval mark and check that the class symbol (e.g. IA or IB) is diametrically opposite the approval number.
